_meta.purpose: Fame signals ESPN does not expose (Pro Bowls, first-team All-Pro, major awards, draft slot, Heisman, general-public profile). Feeds NflPlayer.fame so easy mode contains recognizable faces, not statistical leaders.
_meta.absentMeans: UNKNOWN, never zero. A player with no entry could not be positively identified on Wikipedia; the scorer must fall back to its other inputs. A present entry with proBowls: 0 is a verified zero.
_meta.targetRule: union of fame>=45 in players.json, every id in clips.json, every round 1-2 pick since 2021, and every player on the NFLPA top-50 sales list

fields.proBowls: Pro Bowl selections, from the Wikipedia infobox highlights list
fields.majorAwards: MVP, Offensive/Defensive Player of the Year, Offensive/Defensive Rookie of the Year, Super Bowl MVP, Comeback Player of the Year, with years
fields.draft: overall pick and year as stated on Wikipedia (cross-checked against players.json)
fields.nationalProfile: 0-3 editorial rating of general-public recognition; 3 is the genuinely famous handful
fields.profileFrom: which anchors produced nationalProfile (starting-qb, nflpa-merch-#N, editorial)
fields.draftConflict: present only where Wikipedia and players.json disagree on the draft slot; players.json is authoritative for the roster
fields.source: the Wikipedia article used and which identity checks agreed

sources.how: en.wikipedia.org MediaWiki API (action=query&prop=revisions&rvslots=main), "Infobox gridiron football biography" highlights list, parsed verbatim

sources.what: nationalProfile floor of 1 for every current starting quarterback
sources.how: Wikipedia, List of current NFL starting quarterbacks (32 teams)

sources.what: nationalProfile floor of 1 (top 50) and 2 (top 10) from what fans actually buy
sources.how: NFLPA Top 50 NFL Player Sales List, March 1 2025 - February 28 2026, compiled from 85+ licensees

sources.what: nationalProfile 2 and 3 above the anchored floor
sources.how: editorial, argued in each entry's notes from national ad campaigns, mainstream (non-sports) coverage and social-following rankings

nationalProfileScale.0: known to followers of the sport only — the honest default
nationalProfileScale.1: a name essentially every NFL viewer knows (anchored: starting QB, or NFLPA top-50 merchandise sales)
nationalProfileScale.2: crosses over past the fanbase — national ad campaigns, top-10 merchandise sales, magazine covers
nationalProfileScale.3: famous to people who do not watch football

notCarried: second-team All-Pro (too weak a fame signal to be worth the false precision)
Super Bowl rings (a team outcome; the roster already implies them)
Pro Bowl alternates/replacements are counted exactly as Wikipedia lists them, never inferred
